q: Does parameter concentration on the single-target class transfer to warm-start / meta-learning QAOA on structured combinatorial problems (MaxCut on random regular graphs, Sherrington-Kirkpatrick), and how much wall-clock optimization is saved by seeding at the concentrated (gamma*, beta*) values vs a cold start?
basis: The paper only proves concentration for the trivial cost H_z = 1 - |t><t|. Whether the concentrated angles are a useful warm-start for interesting combinatorial cost Hamiltonians is the natural next question and is what makes concentration operationally useful, not just mathematically true.
next_steps: Run QAOA at p=1..5 on 3-regular MaxCut, n=8..20, comparing (i) L-BFGS-B from cold random seeds, (ii) L-BFGS-B seeded at paper's (pi(n+2)/(n+4), pi/(n+2)), (iii) same seed but rescaled by graph-averaged edge weight. Report median iterations-to-convergence and final approximation ratio. Use qiskit-aer statevector, CPU only, free.

q: Under what precise conditions does parameter concentration FAIL? Specifically: does concentration break down for heterogeneous target-state ensembles (mixed Hamming weight, non-projector cost Hamiltonians), and can that breakdown be predicted from a single scalar (spectral gap of H_z, effective dimension of the reachable manifold)?
basis: The paper proves concentration for a rank-1 projector cost. Real problems have full-spectrum cost Hamiltonians; if concentration is a projector-specific artifact, warm-start use is limited. No published characterization of the failure boundary exists.
next_steps: Sweep synthetic cost Hamiltonians H_z = sum_k lambda_k |k><k| with controlled spectral gap Delta and effective rank r, run QAOA at p=1..3, measure Delta^2 vs n for each (Delta, r). Fit crossover where Delta^2 saturates. All statevector, n<=14, seconds each. Free.

q: Can symmetry-informed initialization (e.g. exploiting problem Z_2, S_n permutation, or graph automorphisms) be composed with parameter concentration to give a strictly better initial guess than concentration alone, and does the combined initialization retain concentration properties?
basis: Recent work (Shaydulin et al. 2021, Egger et al. 2021 warm-start QAOA) shows symmetry-based initialization helps independently. Whether the two effects stack multiplicatively, additively, or interfere destructively is unaddressed.
next_steps: On Z_2-symmetric MaxCut instances (bipartite, regular), initialize at (gamma_conc, beta_conc) with an additional symmetric rotation from the problem's automorphism group. Measure optimizer iterations to 99% of optimum vs pure concentration seed and vs pure symmetry seed. p=1..3, n=8..16, statevector, free.

q: How robust is the concentrated parameter transfer under realistic NISQ noise (single/two-qubit depolarizing, T1/T2, readout error), and does the noise-adjusted optimal angle track the noiseless concentrated value or drift systematically as noise strength grows?
basis: The paper is pure theory (exact statevector). Practical value of parameter transfer hinges on whether concentrated angles remain near-optimal under noise or whether every hardware calibration needs its own optimization. This is testable entirely in simulation with qiskit-aer noise models.
next_steps: For n=6..10, p=1..3, sweep depolarizing error rate p_err in {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} using qiskit-aer AerSimulator with noise model. Re-optimize (gamma, beta) at each p_err, compute |theta_noisy - theta_concentrated| vs p_err. Plot drift trajectory. Free, CPU-only, ~minutes per point.

q: Can a small ML model (2-layer MLP, kernel ridge regression, or a Gaussian process) be trained on (n, p, problem-feature-vector) -> (gamma*, beta*) using a modest catalog of solved instances, and does it generalize to unseen n or unseen problem classes at accuracy sufficient to replace an optimizer?
basis: If concentration means the target manifold is low-dimensional in the (n, p, problem-descriptor) space, direct ML prediction of optimal angles should be feasible and would eliminate optimization entirely. This is a natural operational extension of the paper's theoretical result.
next_steps: Build a corpus of 300 solved (n, p, edge-density, spectral-gap) -> (gamma*, beta*) tuples for MaxCut n=6..14, p=1..3 using the sweep code already in this replication. Train an sklearn KernelRidge model with RBF kernel; evaluate leave-one-instance-class-out MAE in radians and downstream approximation-ratio loss. Free, CPU only.
